record.paper_title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems
record.original_question: Let Φ^t: Ω → Ω be an open dynamical system, with t discrete for maps and continuous for flows, and let H ⊂ Ω be a hole through which trajectories are absorbed. For an initial measure μ0, let Ω_t be the survivor set of points whose trajectories do not enter H during (0,t], let P(t)=μ0(Ω_t) be the survival probability, and let γ be the exponential escape rate when it exists. If μ∞ is a conditionally invariant limiting survivor measure and ν is the natural invariant measure on the repeller, how generally does the escape-rate formula γ = sum of the positive Lyapunov exponents minus the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy h_KS, with the quantities computed with respect to ν, remain valid, especially beyond uniformly hyperbolic maps and for flows?

evidence.quote: The conditionally invariant measure μ∞ is supported on the set of points with infinite past avoiding the hole
Pesin’s formula generalises in the open case to the “escape rate formula” [28, 37] γ = ∑ i:λi>0 λi − hKS (6) where the quantities on the right hand side are defined with respect to ν.
Open problem 1. How general is the escape rate formula, Eq. (6)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Phi^t:\Omega\to\Omega$ be a dynamical system on a state space $\Omega$, where $t$ ranges over the non-negative integers (in the discrete-time case) or the non-negative reals (in the continuous-time case). Fix a measurable subset $H\subset\Omega$ (the "hole") and an initial probability measure $\mu_0$ on $\Omega$. For $t\ge 0$ define the survivor set
$$\Omega_t=\{x\in\Omega:\Phi^s(x)\notin H\ \text{for all}\ 0<s\le t\}$$
and the survival probability $P(t)=\mu_0(\Omega_t)$. When the limit
$$\gamma=-\lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{1}{t}\log P(t)$$
exists and is positive, it is called the (exponential) escape rate. Assume there exists a conditionally invariant limiting survivor measure $\mu_\infty$ (i.e. a probability measure satisfying $\Phi^t_*\mu_\infty=e^{-\gamma t}\mu_\infty$ on $\Omega\setminus H$) and an associated natural invariant measure $\nu$ supported on the noninvasive repeller (the set of points whose forward and backward orbits avoid $H$). Let $\{\lambda_i\}$ denote the Lyapunov exponents of $\nu$ and let $h_{KS}(\nu)$ denote its Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy.

Determine the most general class of open dynamical systems for which the escape rate formula
$$\gamma=\sum_{i:\lambda_i>0}\lambda_i-h_{KS}(\nu)$$
holds. In particular, establish (or refute) its validity beyond the setting of uniformly hyperbolic maps, including non-uniformly hyperbolic maps with singularities and continuous-time flows.
artifact.category_tag: open dynamical systems and escape rates
artifact.status_search_result: The escape-rate formula is established as an equality for uniformly hyperbolic systems and for systems admitting Markov tower extensions with spectral gaps (e.g., work generalizing Eckmann–Ruelle/Pesin to open systems, including results of Demers–Wright–Young and others). General upper bounds on the escape rate hold for diffeomorphisms with singularities and arbitrary holes, but matching lower bounds—and hence equality—are not known in full generality, and the case of flows and broad non-uniformly hyperbolic settings remains only partially settled.

status_evidence.title: Entropy, Lyapunov Exponents and Escape Rates in Open Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Upper bounds for escape rates are proved for general diffeomorphisms with singularities; lower bounds and the equality with positive Lyapunov exponents minus entropy are obtained for systems admitting Markov tower extensions with spectral gaps.
status_evidence.claim: The escape rate formula is proven in general settings only as an inequality; equality is known under additional structural assumptions such as Markov tower extensions with spectral gaps.

status_evidence.title: Open systems and escape rates
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the escape-rate formalism relating escape rates to Lyapunov exponents and KS entropy on the repeller.
status_evidence.claim: The formula is classical in the uniformly hyperbolic / Axiom A setting.
